        ADG Redis Projection Integrity Tests.

        Validates the zero-loss projection invariant:
          SQLite = canonical source of truth
          Redis  = deterministic, lossless projection

        Test inventory
        --------------
        Test 1: projection_completeness ù every SQLite edge has a corresponding
                adg:edge_detail:<id> HASH in Redis with all fields preserved.
        Test 2: metadata_integrity ù adg:meta HASH contains all required fields
                including sqlite_digest, redis_digest, and projection_coherent.
        Test 3: adjacency_consistency ù for every edge, edge_id appears in the
                correct adg:edge:<src>:<rel> and adg:edge:in:<tgt>:<rel> sets.
        Test 4: replay_determinism ù running ingest twice with --force produces
                identical sqlite_digest values (deterministic hash).
        Test 5: module_context_precomputation ù modules with edges have
                precomputed context blobs in adg:module_context:<id>.
        Test 6: violations_id_projection ù violation IDs in adg:violations LIST

      <Module test_negative_control_exit0_tamper.py>
        <Function test_negative_control_integrity>
          Validates the integrity of the negative control system.

          This test enforces Guarantee #25. When the `W4_NEGCTRL_TAMPER` environment
          variable is set to '1', this test is designed to fail. The `pytest.mark.xfail`
          decorator with `strict=True` ensures two things:
          1. If the test fails as expected (in tamper mode), it is marked as XFAIL.
          2. If the test unexpectedly passes (meaning the tamper was not detected), the
             test run fails.

          Crucially, a test run with an XFAIL result exits with code 0, allowing CI
          to verify the tamper detection mechanism without failing the build.
